title: Don't forget your game needs to actually be fun to play
author: ImportGuy
selftext:
I think as tools continue to get better and prototyping faster, it's easy to lose sight of the fact that games are for the enjoyment of people and at their very core need to actually be fun.

It seems like there's a lot of questions on the sub about "should I continue" or "is it worth the investment: and I know most people are just playing around and don't intend to bring a game to market but, if you are in anyway, serious about leveraging new tooling for an actual game, you need to keep in mind and ask the question: **do you like playing it?**

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body: Yeah I mean so many people are just building to learn or building for the sake of building.  Building itself has become kind of like a game.

replies.author: ClibeanCeann
replies.body: I refuse to call generating games with AI "building". Only if you are doing a lot of the manual work like modelling, animating, programming. At least one of these skills you're actually doing.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: I don't think drawing a distinction between manual and automated code authorship will be a thing anyone does in a few years.  Kind of a relic of the early 20s, when both systems exist side by side.

replies.author: ClibeanCeann
replies.body:
I know what you mean. And just as with technology advancements in history, we have come further away from machine level instructions like literal wires and binary, to low level languages, to high level languages, to now plain english (AI prompts). However, all of the previous iterations actually took effort and logical thinking. Now I can probably prompt an AI with "make a fart game" and it has a very good chance to one shot fully generate a game.   
  
This is so drastically different. Even though I graduated with a computer science degree and became a professional developer over the past 10 years, I still had to know a fair amount about how machines work, low level languages and hardware. During my education even fundamentals of machines and computing that haven't changed since the early days is a huge benefit to programming with high level languages, to understand optimisation at the minimum.

Now, NONE of that is required, You just prompt it to "make it work".

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
That's not really true man, idk if you're new to this or what, but many of the devs in this sub are creating very intentional, multi-layered systems and detailed specifications to build these games.  Sure you might get plenty of dummies one-shotting slop demos but that's the noise, not the signal.

Everyone wants to say LLM based tools are a sea change that defies all other technological advances, but I'm not buying it.  I don't slide into that way of thinking, the sci fi "AI vs human" kind of thinking that questions whether what we make using AI tools is made by us or made by some kind of machine organism.  The more I learn about how LLMs and agentic systems work, the more I really think that's all just sci fi and hype.

replies.author: ClibeanCeann
replies.body: By no means am I new to it, I use AI daily at work as it's pretty much mandatory now. I agree there's a lot of misunderstandings and I do understand how LLMs work. It's a large language model. Clue is in the name. It processes languages fast. I'm pretty sure we are agreeing, but my point still stands. I already described the "dummies" you are talking about, those making slop. But that is actually the majority of people, and many of them think they are "building" - which is my point.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
Yeah maybe majority, who knows.  Plenty of people lazily generating derivative work and being like "wow it made a clone of x" 

People always copied and pasted templates and configured pre built software too.  This is like... A wetter version of that.

But there are very legit ways to use these tools that involve intentional systems design and engineering.

comments.author: Destituted
comments.body:
I like AI building my games because I kind of get to see it as a fresh player going in sometimes.

Honestly working on a game for over a year and playing it nonstop you start to lose sight of how a new player feels in it, so in that sense AI has been kind of cool.

When you know all of the possibilities, what it’s like to reach max power, teleport to any map or area, etc it’s hard to rekindle that feeling with your own game for yourself as a real player.

comments.author: adelie42
comments.body:
I do appreciate this and I kind of love that game development has become about as easy as writing a book. And even before AI there are tons of terrible games (and books), and just imagine you could be just as terrible as them!

But seriously, I am using cowork form my phone for a lot when I have downtime at work for a game I am working on, and part of what is slowing me down is having too much fun playing it :)

And honestly, so much in the past decade seems like the same recycled garbage that AI is going to empower people with really great ideas to solo develop something uniquely fun because the barrier to coding has only continued to fall. This sub is living proof.

comments.author: Equivalent_Bird
comments.body: Totally agreed. I've spent nearly a year of tokens, but I still have to manually design the gameplay, mechanics and writing the narrative and the lore framework on my own. Game Design is challenging even for humans, while AI is capable in assets generation and game design description, it just lack of the experience layer like a human, and technically lack of enough training data of what 'fun' means in codebase. Indeed it can easily reproduce something like GTA or Minecraft, that's because there are game screenshots, videos and community discussions as training data, but it's not quite easy to create anything new and complex in simple prompts. That's why I have spent so much time and energy. So far I still haven't recorded the game video, just set up the Steam page with the images from older builds for review. Hopefully it will be finished soon. (not self-promoting here)
